title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the stratification 'at infinity' of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification M̂_{g,ν} = M̄_{g,ν}, viewed fibrewise over Spec Z. The strata M_G are indexed by stable dual graphs, which he calls 'MD-graphes' (Mumford–Deligne). Ĝ_M denotes the closure of a stratum and M̂_G^∞ = M̂_G \ M_G its boundary. The proposition stated at the end of p.71 is: if dim M_G ≥ 2, then M̂_G^∞ is connected, fibre by fibre.

Step 1, reduction to one factor. By (89), M̂_G is (up to the gluing/finite map) the product over the vertices α of compactified moduli spaces M̂^!_{g_α,ν̂_α}. Here ν̂_α counts the marked points plus the branch points at α. The open stratum M_G is the product of the open parts. Each factor is connected. Write X = ∏ X_α. Its boundary is ∪_α (X_1 × … × ∂X_α × … ). Every factor of dimension ≥ 1 has nonempty boundary, which he says explicitly. So if at least two factors have dim ≥ 1, the pieces pairwise meet in the products of boundaries, and the boundary is connected. Otherwise all but one factor are points, and one reduces to a single M̂_{g,ν} = M̄_{g,I} with N = dim = 3(g−1)+ν ≥ 2.

Step 2, low dimension. The case N = 2 (M̄_{0,5}, M̄_{1,2}) is said to be already done, so one may assume N ≥ 3.

Step 3, chain argument. The boundary is a union of irreducible, connected boundary divisors. It suffices to show that any two can be joined by a chain of boundary divisors in which consecutive members intersect. The divisors are listed as one-edge MD-graphs (90):
- (a) the irreducible-node divisor Δ_irr: one vertex of genus g−1 with a loop, carrying all of I (exists if g ≥ 1).
- (b) Δ_{g',I'}: two vertices of genus g', g'' joined by an edge, with I = I' ⊔ I'' and g'+g'' = g. Stability requires card I' ≥ 2 when g' = 0, and likewise for g''.

The next page carries out the argument. Common two-edge degenerations of (a) and (b) are used when g ≥ 1. For g = 0 the chains b'' of genus-0 vertices are used, i.e. paths in the graph of boundary divisors of M̄_{0,n}.

The problem this serves is the topology of the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. The connectedness of boundary strata is presumably used for statements about the Teichmüller tower and fundamental groupoids at infinity.
errors: In the image, the condition under (90b) appears to read 'g'+g''=0'. This is an evident slip for g'+g''=g, which the transcription already gives.

(89) writes M̂_G ≃ ∏ M̂^!_{g_α,ν̂_α}. Strictly, the closure of a stratum is only the image of this product under a finite map: quotient by graph automorphisms, plus non-normal gluing along nodes. Connectedness of the boundary is preserved under surjective maps, so the argument is unaffected.

The product argument needs that every factor of dimension ≥ 1 has nonempty boundary, which Grothendieck notes explicitly. It also needs that a zero-dimensional factor is a point with empty boundary. Both hold. The proof is otherwise sound in outline.

ideas.what: Boundary of the closure of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n} is connected as soon as its dimension is ≥ 2; proved via the product decomposition of strata closures and a chain argument on boundary divisors.
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of the boundary complex / tropical moduli space Δ_{g,n}; connectedness of the dual complex of the DM boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. Connectivity of the curve complex is due to Harvey and Harer. For the boundary complex Δ_{g,n}: Chan–Galatius–Payne, and Allcock–Corey–Payne (who show simple connectivity).
ideas.where_published: Not as such. Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the stratification at infinity of M_{g,ν} only qualitatively.

ideas.what: Description of boundary divisors of M̄_{g,I} by one-edge stable ('MD') graphs, with the stability condition card I' ≥ 2 when g' = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary divisors Δ_irr and Δ_{h,S} of M̄_{g,n}

ideas.what: Closure of a stratum M_G is (finitely covered by) the product of compactified moduli spaces attached to the vertices of G.
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / clutching morphisms ξ_G : ∏_v M̄_{g_v,n_v} → M̄_{g,n}

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine proof of the connectedness of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}, a fact well known in the later literature (dual complex and tropical moduli connectivity). Its interest is mainly as evidence of Grothendieck's systematic 'MD-graph' combinatorics of the boundary over Z, with no new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: the image reads 'est connexe dès que parmi les facteurs M̂^!_{g_α,ν̂_α}, il y en a au moins deux qui sont de dim ≥ 1', not 'pour l'un des facteurs'.
The line 'le cas Γ̂[?] le cas ≐ 3(g−1)+ν=2 est déjà vu, dans DPS N≥3' should read roughly 'le cas où 3(g−1)+ν = 2 est déjà vu, donc DPS N ≥ 3' (donc = 'thus', DPS likely = 'on peut supposer').
'diviseurs à l'infini peuvent être joints par une chaîne de tels div. deux à deux consécutifs ayant une intersection non vide': 'et une' should be 'ayant une'.
In (90b) the image seems to show 'g'+g''=0' (an author slip for g).
